Configure parallel worker threads for large-network inference

rgraphtool_threads.Rd

Query and configure the portable C++23 thread pool used to parallelize large-network stochastic block model minimization in minimize_blockmodel_dl, refine_blockmodel_dl, and minimize_nested_blockmodel_dl.

Usage

rgraphtool_max_threads()
rgraphtool_num_threads()
rgraphtool_set_num_threads(nthreads)

Arguments

nthreads

Positive integer number of worker threads (capped at 256), or "auto" to use rgraphtool_max_threads().

Details

rgraphtool uses a built-in C++23 std::thread pool rather than OpenMP, so multithreading works identically on macOS (including Apple clang without libomp), Linux, and Windows with no external threading library. Worker threads never call the R API or R's RNG; per-thread deterministic xoshiro256** generators are seeded from R's RNG on the main thread before entering parallel regions, so results remain reproducible under set.seed() for a fixed thread count.

By default rgraphtool runs on 1L thread so background tasks and shared systems are never oversubscribed unexpectedly. Opt in globally via rgraphtool_set_num_threads(k) or options(rgraphtool.nthreads = k), or per call via the nthreads argument.

In practice, 4–16 threads typically provide the best speedups (roughly 3x–4.3x on networks with \(N = 10^4\)–\(10^5\) vertices), after which sequential priority-queue merge commits limit further scaling; 32–64 threads still give incremental gains on \(N \ge 10^5\) networks. To reduce peak RAM on very large networks, lower options(rgraphtool.q_cache_max = 1000) (the default 5000 uses ~100 MB for the exact partition-count table) and pair multithreading with strictly agglomerative search (control = list(bisection = FALSE, r = 0.5)) or hierarchy-shape initialization (simple_init = TRUE).

Value

rgraphtool_max_threads() returns the number of hardware threads reported by std::thread::hardware_concurrency() (at least 1L).

rgraphtool_num_threads() returns the active default thread count.

rgraphtool_set_num_threads() invisibly returns the configured integer thread count.

See also

minimize_blockmodel_dl, minimize_nested_blockmodel_dl, demo("large_networks")

Examples

rgraphtool_max_threads()
#> [1] 10
old <- rgraphtool_num_threads()
rgraphtool_set_num_threads(min(2L, rgraphtool_max_threads()))
rgraphtool_num_threads()
#> [1] 2
rgraphtool_set_num_threads(old)
